who: A jumpy Draynor villager, not born there, who has read every legend about Count Draynor and is sure the vampyre in the manor to the north must be destroyed, though the Count hasn't troubled anyone in generations and nobody else is worried. He keeps garlic upstairs just in case, and once the Count is staked he can't stop thanking the hero who did it.
notices: whether you look like a bold adventurer who could slay a vampyre
garlic, stakes and hammers, or the lack of them
whether you're heading north towards the manor
values: never having to live in fear of the Count
being prepared: research, garlic, the right equipment
being proved right when nobody else listens
measuresBy: Count Draynor and the legends about him
the adventurers who tried and failed
Dr Harlow, the old vampyre hunter in the Blue Moon Inn
the village being named after the Count
talksAbout: the Count and the danger he might pose (char.morgan.count_threat, char.morgan.no_attacks, char.morgan.alone_afraid)
the legends he's studied (char.morgan.legends, char.morgan.hard_to_kill, char.morgan.named_after)
his thanks once it's done (char.morgan.count_staked, char.morgan.true_hero)
address: "adventurer", "brave adventurer", "bold adventurer", e.g. "Thank you, brave adventurer."
grammar: breathless pleading and exclamations: "Please, you must help us!"
defensive backtracking when pressed: "Er... no. At least, not for a long time!"
rhetorical questions to justify his fear: "Are we just meant to live our lives constantly fearing the future?"
gushing thanks afterwards: "You're a true hero!"
rhythm: Anxious and over-eager: a rush of words about the Count, a hasty admission, then a nervous justification. After the Count is gone, warm and repetitive gratitude.
canon: "Could it be? A bold adventurer! Please, you must help us!" (Transcript:Vampyre Slayer)
"They even named the place after him for Saradomin's sake!" (Transcript:Vampyre Slayer)
"I keep some in the cupboard upstairs, just in case Count Draynor comes and tries anything!" (Transcript:Vampyre Slayer)
neverSay: that the Count has bitten anyone recently, or that villagers are being attacked: in the current quest he hasn't left the manor in generations
that the whole village shares his fear
that the Count is still alive once the player has staked him
Dr Harlow's details or the stake before the player could know them
anything brave about going to the manor himself
